fish.subject: Neon tetra (Paracheirodon innesi). A tiny slender torpedo-shaped freshwater fish, brilliant iridescent turquoise blue stripe from eye to tail, bright scarlet red stripe along the REAR HALF of its lower body, pearly silver belly, olive translucent back, large realistic dark eye rimmed with silver. Small clear-grey dorsal and forked tail fins, graceful thin body, no whiskers.

Harlequin rasbora (Trigonostigma heteromorpha). Warm copper peach pink reflective scales, a deeper diamond-shaped body, the distinctive large sharp BLACK TRIANGULAR WEDGE on the rear half of its side that tapers to the tail, bright amber eye with dark pupil, delicate orange-red dorsal and deeply forked tail fins. Elegant natural aquarium fish, no whiskers.

Peppered cory catfish (Corydoras paleatus). A small stocky bottom-dwelling armored catfish, pale bronze silver body with irregular dark charcoal and olive peppered mottled patches on both sides, clearly defined overlapping armor plates, rounded blunt snout and small dark eye, short fine barbels beside the mouth. High triangular dorsal fin, broad paired pectoral fins, speckled fan-shaped tail, cream belly. Low wedge body silhouette, natural anatomy.

Pearl gourami (Trichopodus leerii). A graceful laterally compressed oval body, bronze and warm silver shimmering scales covered in many distinct tiny cream PEARL SPOTS, a thin dark horizontal stripe from mouth through eye to tail, a warm burnt orange throat and chest. Long elegant dorsal and anal fins with fine delicate rays and pearl pattern, rounded lyre-like tail, two characteristic long thin pelvic feelers beneath the body. A realistic healthy freshwater gourami, peaceful and regal.
